title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第二十一: 魏徵 Volume 71 Biographies 21: Wei Zheng

sentences.zh: ○蘇世長 子良嗣

translations.literal: ○ Su Shichang; his son Liangsi
translations.idiomatic: ● Su Shichang; his son Liangsi

sentences.zh: 韋雲起 孫方質

translations.literal: Wei Yunqi; Sun Fangzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunqi; Sun Fangzhi

sentences.zh: 孫伏伽　張玄素蘇世長蘇世長，雍州武功人也。

translations.literal: Sun Fuyi; Zhang Xuansu. Su Shichang—Su Shichang was a native of Wugong in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fuyi; Zhang Xuansu. Su Shichang was from Wugong in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖彤，後魏直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tong was a Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong had served the Northern Wei as a Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父振，周宕州刺史、建威縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Governor of Dangzhou under Zhou and Marquis of Jianwei County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had been Governor of Dangzhou under the Northern Zhou and Marquis of Jianwei.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，世長年十餘歲，上書言事。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, Shichang was a little more than ten years old and submitted a memorial on public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While still a boy of about ten under Emperor Wu of Zhou, Shichang submitted a memorial on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其年小，召問：「讀何書？」

translations.literal: The Emperor, because he was young, summoned him and asked, "What books have you read?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought him very young and summoned him to ask, "What books have you read?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「讀《孝經》、《論語》。」

translations.literal: He replied, "I have read the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects."

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「《孝經》、《論語》何所言？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "What do the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects say?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What do those books say?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「《孝經》云：『為國者不敢侮於鰥寡。』

translations.literal: He replied, "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'He who governs the state does not dare to slight widowers and widows.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Classic of Filial Piety says that one who governs a state must not slight widowers and widows.

sentences.zh: 《論語》云：『為政以德。』

translations.literal: The Analects says, 'To govern is to rely on virtue."
translations.idiomatic: And the Analects says that to govern is to rely on virtue.

sentences.zh: 」武帝善其對，令於獸門館讀書。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his answer and ordered him to study at the Beast-Gate Lodge."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with his answer and had him study at the Beast-Gate Lodge."

sentences.zh: 以其父歿王事，因令襲爵，世長於武帝前擗踴號泣，武帝為之改容。

translations.literal: Because his father had died in the service of the state, he was ordered to succeed to the title; before the Emperor, Shichang beat his breast and wailed until the Emperor's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ordered to inherit his father's title because his father had died in royal service, Shichang beat his breast and wept before the emperor until the emperor's face softened.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，世長又屢上便宜，頗有補益，超遷長安令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Shichang again repeatedly submitted timely proposals, with considerable benefit, and was promoted out of turn to Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Shichang again submitted many timely memorials that proved useful, and he was promoted ahead of schedule to Magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為都水少監，使於上江督運。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was Vice Director of the Directorate of Waterways and was sent to the Upper Yangtze to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he served as Vice Director of Waterways and was dispatched to the upper Yangtze to supervise shipping.

sentences.zh: 會江都難作，世長為煬帝發喪慟哭，哀感路人。

translations.literal: When the catastrophe at Jiangdu occurred, Shichang held mourning for Emperor Yang and wept bitterly, moving passersby to grief.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil broke out at Jiangdu, Shichang mourned Emperor Yang with bitter weeping that moved everyone who passed by.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭號，署為太子太保、行台右僕射。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he appointed him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Right Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, having seized power, appointed him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Right Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與世充兄子弘烈及將豆盧褒俱鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Together with Shichong's nephew Honglie and the general Doulu Bao he garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Xiangyang together with Shichong's nephew Honglie and the general Doulu Bao.

sentences.zh: 時弘烈娶褒女為妻，深相結托。

translations.literal: At that time Honglie had married Bao's daughter and they were deeply bound in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie had by then married Bao's daughter, and the two men were closely allied.

sentences.zh: 高祖與褒有舊，璽書諭之，不從，頻斬使者。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had old ties with Bao and sent an imperial letter to instruct him; he would not obey and repeatedly executed envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, who had known Bao of old, sent sealed instructions, but Bao refused to submit and repeatedly executed the envoys.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，洛陽平，世長首勸弘烈歸降。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, when Luoyang was pacified, Shichang was the first to urge Honglie to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4, after Luoyang fell, Shichang was the first to urge Honglie to submit.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，高祖誅褒而責世長來晚之故，世長頓顙曰：「自古帝王受命，為逐鹿之喻，一人得之，萬夫斂手。

translations.literal: When they reached the capital, the Founding Emperor executed Bao and reproached Shichang for coming late; Shichang bowed his forehead to the ground and said, "From antiquity the receiving of the Mandate by emperors and kings has been likened to chasing deer—when one man obtains it, ten thousand men lay down their hands.
translations.idiomatic: After they reached the capital, the Founding Emperor executed Bao and blamed Shichang for his late submission. Shichang kowtowed and said, "Since antiquity the winning of empire has been likened to a deer hunt: once one man takes the prize, all the rest must stand down.

sentences.zh: 豈有獲鹿之後，忿同獵之徒，問爭肉之罪也？

translations.literal: How could there be, after the deer is taken, anger at fellow hunters and inquiry into the crime of quarreling over the meat?
translations.idiomatic: Surely there is no precedent for punishing one's fellow hunters once the deer is already in hand.

sentences.zh: 陛下應天順人，布德施惠，又安得忘管仲、雍齒之事乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has responded to Heaven and followed the people, spreading virtue and bestowing grace—how could you forget the affairs of Guan Zhong and Yong Chi!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has answered Heaven and won the people, spreading virtue far and wide—will you not remember how Guan Zhong and Yong Chi were treated?

sentences.zh: 且臣武功之士，經涉亂離，死亡略盡，惟臣殘命，得見聖朝，陛下若復殺之，是絕其類也。

translations.literal: Moreover, I am a man of Wugong; having passed through turmoil and separation, death has nearly taken us all—only my remnant life remains to behold the holy dynasty; if Your Majesty kills me again, you will extinguish our kind.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I am from Wugong, a place ravaged by war until nearly all my kin are dead; only I survive to see this enlightened reign. If Your Majesty kills me now, you will wipe out what is left of my house.

sentences.zh: 實望天恩，使有遺種。」

translations.literal: I truly hope for Heaven's grace that there may be descendants left."
translations.idiomatic: I beg only that Heaven's grace leave some remnant of my line.

sentences.zh: 高祖與之有故，笑而釋之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had old ties with him, laughed, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, who knew him of old, laughed and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 尋授玉山屯監。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Supervisor of the Yushan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Supervisor of the Yushan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 後於玄武門引見，語及平生，恩意甚厚。

translations.literal: Later he was received in audience at the Xuanwu Gate; they spoke of his whole life, with very deep favor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was received at the Xuanwu Gate, where they spoke of his whole life with great warmth.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿自謂諂佞耶，正直耶？」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "Do you call yourself fawning and sycophantic, or upright?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor asked, "Do you take yourself for a flatterer, or for an honest man?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣實愚直。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject is truly dull and blunt."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am simply dull and blunt, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿若直，何為背世充而歸我？」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "If you are upright, why did you turn your back on Shichong and come to me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If you are so upright, why did you abandon Shichong and come to me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「洛陽既平，天下為一，臣智窮力屈，始歸陛下。

translations.literal: He replied, "Luoyang is already pacified and the realm is one; your subject's wits were exhausted and strength spent—only then did I come to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Only after Luoyang fell and the realm was united—when I had exhausted every stratagem and every resource—did I submit to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 向使世充尚在，臣據漢南，天意雖有所歸，人事足為勍敵。」

translations.literal: Had Shichong still been alive and I held the south of Han, though Heaven's intent might have had its direction, human affairs would have been enough to make a formidable foe."
translations.idiomatic: Had Shichong still lived while I held the Han River southlands, Heaven's favor might still have inclined to you, but on the ground I would have remained a formidable enemy."

sentences.zh: 高祖大笑。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 嘗嘲之曰：「名長意短，口正心邪，棄忠貞於鄭國，忘信義於吾家。」

translations.literal: He once mocked him, saying, "Long in name but short in intent, upright in mouth but crooked in heart—you abandoned loyalty in the state of Zheng and forgot faith toward our house."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor teased him: "Long in name but short in purpose; honest in speech but crooked at heart—you left your loyalty in Zheng and forgot your obligations to us.

sentences.zh: 世長對曰：「名長意短，實如聖旨；

translations.literal: Shichang replied, "Long in name but short in intent—that is truly as the holy edict says;
translations.idiomatic: Shichang replied, "Long in name but short in purpose—that much is exactly as Your Majesty says;

sentences.zh: 口正心邪，未敢奉詔。

translations.literal: upright in mouth but crooked in heart—I dare not accept that edict.
translations.idiomatic: but as for honest in speech yet crooked at heart, I dare not accept that part of the edict.

sentences.zh: 昔竇融以河西降漢，十世封侯；

translations.literal: Formerly Dou Rong surrendered Hexi to Han and his line was enfeoffed as marquises for ten generations;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Dou Rong surrendered the Hexi region to Han and his house was enfeoffed as marquises for ten generations;

sentences.zh: 臣以山南歸國，惟蒙屯監。」

translations.literal: your subject, returning to the state from south of the mountains, has received only a garrison supervisor's post."
translations.idiomatic: yet I, returning from the lands south of the mountains, have received only a garrison supervisor's post."

sentences.zh: 即日擢拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: That same day he was promoted and appointed Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he was promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 從幸涇陽校獵，大獲禽獸於旌門。

translations.literal: He accompanied the hunt at Jingyang and took a great haul of birds and beasts before the banner gate.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on a hunt at Jingyang, where a great catch of game was driven before the banner gate.

sentences.zh: 高祖入御營，顧謂朝臣曰：「今日畋樂乎？」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor entered the imperial camp and, turning to the court ministers, said, "Was today's hunt enjoyable?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor entered camp and asked the ministers, "Was today's hunt a pleasure?

sentences.zh: 世長進曰：「陛下遊獵，薄廢萬機，不滿十旬，未為大樂。」

translations.literal: Shichang advanced and said, "Your Majesty's excursion in hunting has lightly set aside the myriad affairs of state; not yet a full hundred days—it is not yet great pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Shichang stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty has set aside the myriad affairs of state for this hunt, and it has not yet lasted even a hundred days—hardly a great pleasure."

sentences.zh: 高祖色變，既而笑曰：「狂態發耶？」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's expression changed; then he laughed and said, "Has your wild manner broken out?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened, then he laughed. "Are you in one of your wild moods again?"

sentences.zh: 世長曰：「為臣私計則狂，為陛下國計則忠矣。」

translations.literal: Shichang said, "By a minister's private reckoning it is wild; by reckoning for Your Majesty's state it is loyal."
translations.idiomatic: Shichang said, "By my private reckoning it may be wild; by the reckoning of Your Majesty's realm it is loyal."

sentences.zh: 及突厥入寇，武功郡縣，多失戶口，是後下詔將幸武功校獵。

translations.literal: When the Turks invaded, Wugong commandery and its counties lost many households; afterward an edict was issued that the emperor would visit Wugong for a hunting excursion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided, Wugong and its counties lost many households. Later an edict announced that the emperor would visit Wugong on a hunting excursion.

sentences.zh: 世長又諫曰：「突厥初入，大為民害，陛下救恤之道猶未發言，乃於其地又縱畋獵，非但仁育之心有所不足，百姓供頓，將何以堪？」

translations.literal: Shichang remonstrated again, saying, "The Turks have only just entered and greatly harm the people; Your Majesty's words of rescue and relief have not yet been spoken, yet in that very place you again let loose the hunt—not only is the heart of humane nurture insufficient, but how can the people's supplies and encampments bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: Shichang remonstrated again: "The Turks have only just arrived and are ravaging the people. Your Majesty has not yet spoken a word of relief, yet you would hunt in that very region. This falls short not only of humane governance but of what the people can endure in supplies and labor.

sentences.zh: 高祖不納。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗引之於披香殿，世長酒酣，奏曰：「此殿隋煬帝所作耶？

translations.literal: On another occasion he was brought to the Puxiang Hall; Shichang, flushed with wine, memorialized, "Was this hall made by Emperor Yang of Sui?
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he was summoned to the Puxiang Hall. Shichang, well into his cups, asked, "Was this hall built by Emperor Yang of Sui?

sentences.zh: 是何雕麗之若此也？」

translations.literal: Why is it carved and adorned to this degree?"
translations.idiomatic: Why is it carved and adorned to such a degree?

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿好諫似真，其心實詐。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "Your remonstrances seem true, but your heart is truly deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your remonstrances sound sincere, but your heart is deceitful.

sentences.zh: 豈不知此殿是吾所造，何須設詭疑而言煬帝乎？」

translations.literal: Do you not know that this hall was built by me—why must you set up a crafty suspicion and speak of Emperor Yang?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you not know that I built this hall myself? Why feign ignorance and speak of Emperor Yang?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣實不知。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject truly did not know.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I truly did not know, Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 但見傾宮鹿台琉璃之瓦，並非受命帝王愛民節用之所為也。

translations.literal: I only see tiles like those of the Tilted Palace and Deer Terrace in glazed glass—this is not what a ruler who has received the Mandate does when he loves the people and practices frugality.
translations.idiomatic: I see only tiles worthy of the Tilted Palace and the Deer Terrace—hardly the work of a Mandate-bearing ruler who loves his people and practices frugality.

sentences.zh: 若是陛下作此，誠非所宜。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty made this, it is truly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty built this, it is truly not fitting.

sentences.zh: 臣昔在武功，幸常陪侍，見陛下宅宇，才蔽風霜，當此之時，亦以為足。

translations.literal: Your subject was formerly at Wugong and often had the fortune to attend; I saw Your Majesty's dwelling, barely sheltering from wind and frost—at that time I also thought it sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: When I was at Wugong I often attended you and saw your dwelling, barely large enough to keep out wind and frost; even then I thought it ample.

sentences.zh: 今因隋之侈，民不堪命，數歸有道，而陛下得之，實謂懲其奢淫，不忘儉約。

translations.literal: Now, because of Sui's extravagance, the people could not bear their lot and repeatedly turned to the Way; Your Majesty obtained it—I truly thought you would chastise their luxury and lewdness and not forget thrift.
translations.idiomatic: The people, crushed under Sui's extravagance, turned again and again to a righteous ruler, and Your Majesty won the throne. I took it that you would punish Sui's excess and never forget thrift.

sentences.zh: 今初有天下，而於隋宮之內，又加雕飾，欲撥其亂，寧可得乎？」

translations.literal: Now, having just obtained the realm, within the Sui palaces you add carving and ornament—wishing to dispel their disorder, can that be achieved?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have only just won the realm and already add ornament within the Sui palaces. How can disorder be dispelled that way?"

sentences.zh: 高祖深然之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 後歷陝州長史、天策府軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Chief Administrator of Shaanzhou and Libationer for Military Counsel of the Heavenly Stratagem Princedom.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chief Administrator of Shaanzhou and as Libationer for Military Counsel at the Heavenly Stratagem Princedom.

sentences.zh: 秦府初開文學館，引為學士。

translations.literal: When the Qin Princedom first opened the Literary Academy, he was brought in as a Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin Princedom first opened its Literary Academy, he was appointed an academician.

sentences.zh: 與房玄齡等一十八人皆蒙圖畫，令文學褚亮為之贊，曰：「軍諮諧噱，超然辯悟。

translations.literal: He and Fang Xuanling and seventeen others were all granted painted portraits; the literary attendant Chu Liang was ordered to compose encomia for them, saying, "Military counsel harmonious in jest, transcendent in debate and insight.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fang Xuanling and seventeen others were all painted for the academy portrait gallery, and the literary attendant Chu Liang was commissioned to write their encomia. Of Shichang he wrote: "In military counsel, witty and apt; in debate, transcendent and clear.

sentences.zh: 正色於庭，匪躬之故。」

translations.literal: Upright in countenance at court—for the sake of not sparing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Upright of bearing in court—for he would not spare himself.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，聘於突厥，與頡利爭禮，不受賂遺，朝廷稱之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was sent on a mission to the Turks; he disputed ritual precedence with Jieli and would not accept bribes or gifts—the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was sent on a mission to the Turks, where he disputed ceremonial precedence with Jieli and refused all bribes and gifts, winning praise at court.

sentences.zh: 出為巴州刺史，覆舟溺水而卒。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Bazhou, capsized his boat, drowned, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Ba Prefecture, where he capsized a boat, drowned, and died.

sentences.zh: 世長機辯有學，博涉而簡率，嗜酒，無威儀。

translations.literal: Shichang was quick-witted and learned, broadly versed yet plain and direct, fond of wine, and without dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was quick-witted and learned, widely read yet plain in manner, fond of wine, and careless of decorum.

sentences.zh: 初在陝州，部內多犯法，世長莫能禁，乃責躬引咎，自撻於都街。

translations.literal: When he was first at Shaanzhou, within his jurisdiction many broke the law and Shichang could not stop it; he therefore blamed himself and accepted guilt, flogging himself in the capital street.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his tenure at Shaanzhou, lawbreaking was widespread and he could not suppress it. He took the blame on himself and publicly flogged himself in the main street of the prefectural capital.

sentences.zh: 伍伯嫉其詭，鞭之見血，世長不勝痛，大呼而走，觀者咸以為笑，議者方稱其詐。

translations.literal: The ward headmen resented his trickery and flogged him until blood showed; Shichang could not bear the pain, cried out loudly, and ran off—the onlookers all took it for laughter, and commentators then called it deceit.
translations.idiomatic: The ward officers, seeing through the performance, flogged him until he bled. Unable to endure the pain, he cried out and fled, to the amusement of the crowd; critics then pronounced the whole affair a sham.

sentences.zh: 子 良嗣子良嗣，高宗時遷周王府司馬。

translations.literal: Son Liangsi. Liangsi—in the time of Emperor Gaozong was transferred to be Chief Commandant of the Zhou King's household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liangsi. Under Emperor Gaozong, Liangsi was appointed Chief Commandant of the Zhou King's household.

sentences.zh: 王時年少，舉事不法，良嗣正色匡諫，甚見敬憚。

translations.literal: The prince was then young and his conduct often unlawful; Liangsi with stern countenance corrected and remonstrated, and was greatly respected and feared.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was still young and often acted improperly; Liangsi remonstrated with stern countenance and was both respected and feared.

sentences.zh: 王府官屬多非其人，良嗣守文檢括，莫敢有犯，深為高宗所稱。

translations.literal: Many of the princely household's officials were not the right men; Liangsi upheld the statutes in inspection and restraint, and none dared offend—he was deeply praised by Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the prince's staff were unfit for their posts, but Liangsi enforced the regulations so strictly that none dared transgress, and Emperor Gaozong spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 遷荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Chief Administrator of the Jingzhou Superior Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Jingzhou Superior Area Command.

sentences.zh: 高宗使宦者緣江采異竹，將於苑中植之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong sent eunuchs along the river to gather exotic bamboo, intending to plant it in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong sent eunuchs along the Yangtze to collect exotic bamboo for planting in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 宦者科舟載竹，所在縱暴。

translations.literal: The eunuchs requisitioned boats to carry the bamboo and everywhere let loose violence.
translations.idiomatic: They requisitioned boats to carry the bamboo and abused their authority wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 還過荊州，良嗣囚之，因上疏切諫，稱：「遠方求珍異以疲道路，非聖人抑己愛人之道。

translations.literal: On their return they passed through Jingzhou; Liangsi imprisoned them and thereby submitted a stern memorial, stating, "Seeking rarities from afar to weary the roads is not the Way of the sage who restrains himself and loves others.
translations.idiomatic: On their return they passed through Jingzhou, where Liangsi imprisoned them and submitted a stern memorial: "To scour distant regions for curios and exhaust the highways is not the way of a sage who restrains himself and loves the people.

sentences.zh: 又小人竊弄威福，以虧皇明。」

translations.literal: Moreover, petty men usurp authority and blessings, to the detriment of the imperial brilliance."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, petty men are usurping authority, to the detriment of Your Majesty's radiance.

sentences.zh: 言甚切直。

translations.literal: His words were very blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: His language was blunt and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，高宗下制慰勉，遽令棄竹於江中。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Gaozong issued an edict of consolation and encouragement and immediately ordered the bamboo cast into the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Gaozong issued an edict of praise and immediately ordered the bamboo thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，為雍州長史。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era he was Chief Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun era he served as Chief Administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時關中大飢，人相食，盜賊縱橫。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong suffered great famine; people ate one another and bandits ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guanzhong was in severe famine; people resorted to cannibalism and bandits roamed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 良嗣為政嚴明，盜發三日內無不擒扌適。

translations.literal: Liangsi's governance was strict and clear; no theft reported went uncaptured within three days.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi governed with strict clarity; no theft reported went uncaptured within three days.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋代王德真為納言，累封溫國公。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he replaced Wang Dezhen as Chief Counselor and was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Wenguo.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Wang Dezhen as Chief Counselor and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenguo.

sentences.zh: 為西京留守，則天賦詩餞送，賞遇甚渥。

translations.literal: As Western Capital Intendant, Empress Wu composed a poem to send him off on his journey; his favor and treatment were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: As Intendant of the Western Capital he was sent off with a poem composed by Empress Wu herself, so generous was her regard for him.

sentences.zh: 時尚方監裴匪躬檢校西苑，將鬻苑中果菜以收其利。

translations.literal: At that time the Director of the Palace Workshops Pei Feigong was inspecting the Western Park and intended to sell the park's fruits and vegetables to reap profit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Feigong, Director of the Palace Workshops, was supervising the Western Park and planned to sell its produce for profit.

sentences.zh: 良嗣駁之曰：「昔公儀相魯，猶能拔葵去織，未聞萬乘之主，鬻其果菜以與下人爭利也。」

translations.literal: Liangsi refuted him, saying, "Formerly when Gongyi served as Chancellor of Lu, he could still uproot the mallow and remove the weaving—one has not heard of a lord of ten thousand chariots selling his fruits and vegetables to compete for profit with his inferiors."
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi objected: "When Gongyi served as chancellor of Lu, he uprooted his mallow patch and dismissed his weaving women. I have never heard of a Son of Heaven selling garden produce to compete for profit with his subjects.

sentences.zh: 匪躬遂止。

translations.literal: Feigong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Feigong abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 無幾，追入都，遷文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to the capital and transferred to Left Chancellor of the Literary Glory Office, of the Third Rank equal to the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital and appointed Left Chancellor of the Literary Glory Office, Third Rank, with concurrent status at the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 載初元年春，罷文昌左相，加位特進，仍依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Zai'chu he was removed as Left Chancellor of the Literary Glory Office, advanced in rank to Special Advancement, and still continued to oversee state affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first Zai'chu year he was relieved as Left Chancellor but advanced to Special Advancement, retaining his role in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 與地官尚書韋方質不協，及方質坐事當誅，辭引良嗣，則天特保明之。

translations.literal: He was not in harmony with Wei Fangzhi, Minister of the Earth Office; when Fangzhi was implicated in a matter and was to be executed, his testimony implicated Liangsi, and Empress Wu specially protected and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was on poor terms with Wei Fangzhi, Minister of the Earth Office. When Fangzhi was condemned to death for an offense and implicated Liangsi in his testimony, Empress Wu personally cleared him.

sentences.zh: 良嗣謝恩拜伏，便不能復起，輿歸其家，詔御醫張文仲、韋慈藏往視疾。

translations.literal: Liangsi bowed in thanks for the grace but could not rise again; he was carried home in a litter, and an edict ordered the imperial physicians Zhang Wenchong and Wei Cizang to go view his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi kowtowed in gratitude but could not rise again and was carried home. The court physicians Zhang Wenchong and Wei Cizang were sent to attend him.

sentences.zh: 其日薨，年八十五。

translations.literal: That same day he died; he was eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same day, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 則天輟朝三日，舉哀於觀風門，敕百官就宅赴吊。

translations.literal: Empress Wu suspended court for three days and held mourning at the Gate for Observing the Winds, ordering the hundred officials to go to his residence to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu suspended court for three days and led mourning at the Gate for Observing the Winds, ordering all officials to attend the funeral at his home.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，益州都督，賜絹布八百段、米粟八百碩，兼降璽書弔祭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Feather Screen of the First Order, Area Commander of Yizhou, eight hundred bolts of silk cloth and eight hundred piculs of grain and millet, together with an imperial letter of condolence and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal, made Area Commander of Yizhou, and granted eight hundred bolts of silk and eight hundred piculs of grain, together with an imperial letter of condolence.

sentences.zh: 其子踐言，太常丞，尋為酷吏所陷，配流嶺南而死。

translations.literal: His son Jianyan was Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; shortly afterward he was framed by a cruel official, sentenced to exile in Lingnan, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianyan, Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, was soon framed by a cruel official, exiled to Lingnan, and died there.

sentences.zh: 追削良嗣官爵，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Liangsi's offices and titles were posthumously stripped and his household property was confiscated and registered.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi's titles were posthumously revoked and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 景龍元年，追贈良嗣司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinglong, Liangsi was posthumously granted the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong year 1, Liangsi was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 踐言子務玄，襲爵溫國公，開元中，為邠王府長史。

translations.literal: Jianyan's son Wuxuan inherited the title Duke of Wenguo; in the Kaiyuan era he was Chief Administrator of the Bin King's household.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyan's son Wuxuan inherited the title Duke of Wenguo and, during the Kaiyuan reign, served as Chief Administrator of the Bin King's household.

sentences.zh: 韋雲起韋雲起，雍州萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Yunqi. Wei Yunqi was a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunqi. Wei Yunqi was from Wannian in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 伯父澄，武德初國子祭酒、綿州刺史。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Cheng, in the beginning of Wude, was Libationer of the Imperial University and Governor of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Cheng, early in the Wude reign, served as Libationer of the Imperial University and Governor of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 雲起，隋開皇中明經舉，授符璽直長。

translations.literal: Yunqi, in the Kaihuang era of Sui, passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Direct Attendant of Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi passed the Mingjing examination in the Kaihuang era of Sui and was appointed Direct Attendant of Seals and Credentials.

sentences.zh: 嘗因奏事，文帝問曰：「外間有不便事，汝可言之。」

translations.literal: Once, while reporting on affairs, Emperor Wen asked, "If there are inconvenient matters outside, you may speak of them."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while presenting a memorial, Emperor Wen asked him, "If anything in the realm is amiss, you may speak of it.

sentences.zh: 時兵部侍郎柳述在帝側，雲起應聲奏曰：「柳述驕豪，未嘗經事，兵機要重，非其所堪，徒以公主之婿，遂居要職。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of War Liu Shu was at the Emperor's side; Yunqi answered immediately and memorialized, "Liu Shu is arrogant and overbearing, never having handled affairs; military affairs are weighty and not what he can bear—only because he is the emperor's son-in-law does he hold a crucial post.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu, Vice Minister of War, stood at the emperor's side. Yunqi spoke up at once: "Liu Shu is arrogant and inexperienced. Military affairs are too weighty for him; he holds a crucial post only because he married the emperor's daughter.

sentences.zh: 臣恐物議以陛下官不擇賢，濫以天秩加於私愛，斯亦不便之大者。」

translations.literal: Your subject fears that public opinion will hold that Your Majesty appoints office without choosing the worthy, recklessly adding Heaven's ranks to private affection—this too is among the greatest inconveniences."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the court will say that Your Majesty appoints men without regard to merit, lavishing Heaven's ranks on private favorites—that would be a grave evil indeed."

sentences.zh: 帝甚然其言，顧謂述曰：「雲起之言，汝藥石也，可師友之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly approved his words and, turning to Shu, said, "Yunqi's words are your medicine and whetstone—you may take him as teacher and friend."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly approved and told Liu Shu, "Yunqi's words are medicine and whetstone to you; treat him as teacher and friend."

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，詔在朝文武舉人，述乃舉雲起，進授通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Renshou an edict ordered civil and military officials at court to recommend men; Shu then recommended Yunqi, who was advanced and appointed Master of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou reign, when the court was ordered to recommend talent, Liu Shu recommended Yunqi, who was promoted to Master of Communications.

sentences.zh: 大業初，改為通事謁者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was changed to Visitor of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye reign he was made Visitor of Communications.

sentences.zh: 又上疏奏曰：「今朝廷之內多山東人，而自作門戶，更相剡薦，附下罔上，共為朋黨。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial, saying, "Now within the court there are many men from east of the mountains who form their own factions, mutually promoting and denouncing, currying favor below and deceiving above, together making cliques.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "The court is full of men from east of the mountains who have formed factions, promoting one another and deceiving their superiors—an organized clique.

sentences.zh: 不抑其端，必傾朝政，臣所以痛心扼腕，不能默已。

translations.literal: If their beginning is not checked, they will surely overturn court governance; your subject therefore clenches his heart and wrings his wrists and cannot keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: Unless this is checked at the root, it will overturn the government. That is why I cannot remain silent, though it pains me to speak.

sentences.zh: 謹件朋黨人姓名及奸狀如左。」

translations.literal: I respectfully append the names of clique members and their wicked conduct as follows."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully append the names of the clique members and their offenses below.

sentences.zh: 煬帝令大理推究，於是左丞郎蔚之、司隸別駕郎楚之並坐朋黨，配流漫頭赤水，余免官者九人。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang ordered the Court of Review to investigate; thereupon Left Assistant Minister Lang Weizhi and Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Metropolitan Area Lang Chuzhi were both convicted of clique membership, sentenced to exile at Mantou on the Chishui River, and nine others were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered the Court of Review to investigate. Left Assistant Minister Lang Weizhi and Metropolitan Vice Censor Lang Chuzhi were convicted of clique membership and exiled to Mantou on the Chishui; nine others were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入抄營州，詔雲起護突厥兵往討契丹部落。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided Yingzhou, an edict ordered Yunqi to lead Turkic troops to attack the Khitan tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided Yingzhou, Yunqi was ordered to lead Turkic troops against the Khitan tribes.

sentences.zh: 啟民可汗發騎二萬，受其處分。

translations.literal: Qimin Khan sent twenty thousand horsemen, subject to his disposal.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin Khan supplied twenty thousand horsemen under Yunqi's command.

sentences.zh: 雲起分為二十營，四道俱引，營相去各一里，不得交雜。

translations.literal: Yunqi divided them into twenty camps, all four routes advancing together, each camp one li apart, not permitted to mingle.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi divided the force into twenty camps advancing in four columns, each camp one li apart, with strict orders against mingling.

sentences.zh: 聞鼓聲而行，聞角聲而止，自非公使，勿得走馬。

translations.literal: At the sound of drums they marched; at the sound of horns they halted; unless on public business, none might gallop.
translations.idiomatic: They marched at the drum and halted at the horn; except on official business, no one might gallop.

sentences.zh: 三令五申之後，擊鼓而發，軍中有犯約者，斬紇幹一人，持首以徇。

translations.literal: After repeated orders and warnings, the drums were struck and they set out; when someone in the army violated the rules, one Göktürk was beheaded and the head displayed to warn the rest.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated warnings, the drums sounded and the army moved out. When a man violated the rules, Yunqi beheaded one Göktürk and displayed the head as an example.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥將帥來入謁之，皆膝行股戰，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Turkic generals came in to pay respects; all crawled on their knees, thighs trembling, none daring to look up.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic commanders came to pay their respects on their knees, trembling, none daring to look up.

sentences.zh: 契丹本事突厥，情無猜忌，雲起既入其界，使突厥詐雲，向柳城郡欲共高麗交易，勿言營中有隋使，敢漏洩者斬之。

translations.literal: The Khitan had long served the Turks and were without suspicion; once Yunqi entered their territory, he had the Turks feign that they were heading to Liucheng Commandery to trade with Goguryeo, and ordered them not to say there was a Sui envoy in camp—whoever leaked would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had long been subject to the Turks and were unsuspecting. Once inside their territory, Yunqi had the Turks pretend they were bound for Liucheng to trade with Goguryeo and forbade mention of a Sui envoy in camp on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 契丹不備。

translations.literal: The Khitan were unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were caught unprepared.

sentences.zh: 去賊營百里，詐引南度，夜復退還，去營五十里，結陣而宿，契丹弗之知也。

translations.literal: A hundred li from the enemy camp he feigned a southward crossing, then at night withdrew again; fifty li from the camp he formed battle lines and encamped—the Khitan did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li from the enemy camp he feigned a crossing to the south, then withdrew by night; fifty li away he formed ranks and encamped, all unknown to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 既明，俱發，馳騎襲之，盡獲其男女四萬口，女子及畜產以半賜突厥，余將入朝，男子皆殺之。

translations.literal: When it was light, all set out, galloping cavalry to strike them, capturing altogether forty thousand men and women; women and livestock were half given to the Turks, the rest sent to court, and the men were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn all attacked by cavalry and captured forty thousand Khitan men and women. Women and livestock were half given to the Turks; the rest were sent to court, and all the men were killed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝大喜，集百官曰：「雲起用突厥而平契丹，行師奇譎，才兼文武，又立朝謇諤，朕今親自舉之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was greatly pleased and gathered the hundred officials, saying, "Yunqi used the Turks to pacify the Khitan; his campaigning is strange and devious, his talent combines civil and military, and in court he is upright and outspoken—I now personally promote him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was delighted and told the officials, "Yunqi used the Turks to crush the Khitan. His tactics are brilliant, his talent spans civil and military affairs, and in court he speaks without fear. I promote him myself.

sentences.zh: 擢為治書御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Imperial Censor for Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Imperial Censor for Documents.

sentences.zh: 雲起乃奏劾曰：「內史侍郎虞世基，職典樞要，寄任隆重；

translations.literal: Yunqi then memorialized an impeachment, saying, "Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji holds office over crucial pivots, with weighty entrusted responsibility;
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi then impeached Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji, who held crucial responsibilities,

sentences.zh: 御史大夫裴蘊，特蒙殊寵，維持內外。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun has received special extraordinary favor and sustains inner and outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, who enjoyed extraordinary favor and controlled affairs within and without the palace.

sentences.zh: 今四方告變，不為奏聞，賊數實多，或減言少。

translations.literal: Now disturbances are reported from the four quarters yet they do not memorialize; the rebels are in fact numerous, yet they sometimes report fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions are reported from every quarter, yet they do not inform the throne; rebel numbers are in fact large, yet they report them as small.

sentences.zh: 陛下既聞賊少，發兵不多，眾寡懸殊，往皆莫克，故使官軍失利，賊黨日滋。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, having heard the rebels are few, sends out not many troops; the disparity between many and few is extreme, and in the past none could overcome—thus government troops lose advantage and rebel bands daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Because Your Majesty hears that rebels are few, too few troops are sent; the odds are hopeless, government armies fail, and rebel bands grow daily.

sentences.zh: 此而不繩，為害將大，請付有司，詰正其罪。」

translations.literal: If this is not punished, the harm will be great; I request they be handed to the appropriate offices to investigate and correct their crimes."
translations.idiomatic: Unless this is punished, the harm will be great. I ask that they be handed to the proper offices to answer for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 大理卿鄭善果奏曰：「雲起詆訾名臣，所言不實，非毀朝政，妄作威權。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo memorialized, "Yunqi slanders and reviles famous ministers; what he says is not true—this is not to destroy court governance but to presumptuously wield authority."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo replied, "Yunqi slanders eminent ministers with false charges; this is not loyal remonstrance but presumptuous abuse of authority."

sentences.zh: 由是左遷大理司直。

translations.literal: For this he was demoted to Direct Clerk of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi was demoted to Direct Clerk of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸揚州，雲起告歸長安，屬義旗入關，於長樂宮謁見。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang visited Yangzhou, Yunqi requested leave to return to Chang'an; just then the righteous banner entered the Pass, and he had an audience at Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang went to Yangzhou, Yunqi took leave to return to Chang'an. The rebel armies were entering the Pass, and he had an audience at Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 義寧元年，授司農卿，封陽城縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yining he was appointed Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yining year 1 he was appointed Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，加授上開府儀同三司，判農圃監事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was additionally granted Superlative Opening of the Office with Golden Seal and Feather Screen of the First Order and concurrently supervised the Directorate of Agricultural Parks.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 1 he was further granted Superlative Opening of the Office with Golden Seal and made concurrent supervisor of the Directorate of Agricultural Parks.

sentences.zh: 是歲，欲大發兵討王世充，雲起上表諫曰：「國家承喪亂之後，百姓流離，未蒙安養，頻年不熟，關內阻飢。

translations.literal: That year, when a great mobilization was planned to attack Wang Shichong, Yunqi submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying, "The state has inherited after mourning and disorder; the people are displaced and have not received settling care; for successive years harvests have failed, and within the Pass hunger obstructs.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as a great campaign against Wang Shichong was planned, Yunqi remonstrated: "The realm has just emerged from chaos. The people are displaced and unrested; harvests have failed for years, and hunger grips the interior.

sentences.zh: 京邑初平，物情未附，鼠竊狗盜，猶為國憂。

translations.literal: The capital region has only just been pacified; popular sentiment is not yet attached; rats stealing and dogs robbing still worry the state.
translations.idiomatic: The capital has only just been pacified and hearts are not yet won; petty thieves and bandits still threaten the realm.

sentences.zh: 盩厔司竹，余氛未殄；

translations.literal: In Zhouzhi and Sizhu, remaining miasma is not yet extinguished;
translations.idiomatic: At Zhouzhi and Sizhu, rebel remnants are not yet destroyed;

sentences.zh: 藍田、谷口，群盜實多。

translations.literal: at Lantian and Gukou, bandit gangs are truly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: and at Lantian and Gukou bandits are truly numerous.

sentences.zh: 朝夕伺間，極為國害。

translations.literal: Morning and evening they watch for openings—an extreme harm to the state.
translations.idiomatic: They watch every moment for an opening and are a grave danger to the state.

sentences.zh: 雖京城之內，每夜賊發。

translations.literal: Even within the capital walls, every night thieves arise.
translations.idiomatic: Even within the capital, robberies occur every night.

sentences.zh: 北有師都，連結胡寇，斯乃國家腹心之疾也。

translations.literal: To the north is Shidu, linked with barbarian raiders—this is the state's ailment at the heart and vitals.
translations.idiomatic: In the north, Shidu is allied with barbarian raiders—that is the gravest threat to the realm.

sentences.zh: 舍此不圖，而窺兵函、洛，若師出之後，內盜乘虛，一旦有變，禍將不小。

translations.literal: To set this aside and instead cast military eyes on Hangu and Luoyang—if after the army marches out internal bandits seize the void, once there is a change, the calamity will not be small.
translations.idiomatic: To ignore this and aim troops at Hangu and Luoyang—once the army marches out, internal bandits will seize their chance. Any upheaval then would bring no small disaster.

sentences.zh: 臣謂王世充遠隔千里，山川懸絕，無能為害，待有餘力，方可討之。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that Wang Shichong is separated by a thousand li, mountains and rivers hanging apart, unable to do harm—wait until there is surplus strength, then he may be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong lies a thousand li away, cut off by mountains and rivers, and cannot harm us. Wait until strength is to spare, then attack him.

sentences.zh: 今內難未弭，且宜弘於度外。

translations.literal: Now internal troubles are not yet quelled; for the time being one should be magnanimous beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Internal troubles are not yet settled; for now Your Majesty should be magnanimous beyond the usual bounds.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，請暫戢兵，務穡勸農，安人和眾。

translations.literal: In your subject's foolish view, I beg to temporarily sheath arms, devote effort to harvest and encourage farming, settle the people and harmonize the masses.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, sheath the sword for now, devote effort to farming, and settle the people.

sentences.zh: 關中小盜，自然寧息。

translations.literal: The petty thieves within the Pass will naturally quiet and cease.
translations.idiomatic: Petty bandits within the Pass will quiet down of themselves.

sentences.zh: 秦川將卒，賈勇有餘，三年之後，一舉便定。

translations.literal: The generals and soldiers of Qinchuan still have surplus courage to sell; three years hence, one stroke will settle all.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of Qinchuan still have courage to spare; in three years one stroke will settle everything.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲速，臣恐未可。」

translations.literal: Now, though you wish speed, your subject fears it cannot yet be done."
translations.idiomatic: Though speed is desired now, I fear the time is not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor then followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 會突厥入寇，詔雲起總領豳、寧已北九州兵馬，便宜從事。

translations.literal: When the Turks invaded, an edict ordered Yunqi to take overall command of the nine prefectures' troops from Bin, Ning, and northward, acting as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded, Yunqi was ordered to command the troops of the nine northern prefectures from Bin and Ning northward, with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 四年，授西麟州刺史，司農卿如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Governor of Xilin Prefecture in the west, retaining his post as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was appointed Governor of Xilin Prefecture while retaining his post as Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 尋代趙郡王孝恭為夔州刺史，轉遂州都督，懷柔夷獠，鹹得眾心。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he replaced Prince Xiaogong of Zhao Commandery as Governor of Kuizhou, then transferred to be Area Commander of Suizhou, soothing and winning the Yi and Liao—all gained his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Prince Xiaogong of Zhao as Governor of Kuizhou, then became Area Commander of Suizhou, where he won over the Yi and Liao peoples and gained their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遷益州行台民部尚書，尋轉行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Minister of the People Department of the Yizhou Mobile Secretariat, then shortly to Minister of the Military Department of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the People Department of the Yizhou Mobile Secretariat, then to Minister of the Military Department.

sentences.zh: 行台僕射竇軌多行殺戮，又妄奏獠反，冀得集兵。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat Dou Gui often carried out killings, and also falsely memorialized that the Liao had rebelled, hoping to gather troops.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Dou Gui often carried out killings and falsely reported Liao rebellions in hopes of gathering troops.

sentences.zh: 因此作威，肆其凶暴，雲起多執不從。

translations.literal: Thereby wielding authority, he indulged his fierce brutality; Yunqi often held firm and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Thus emboldened, Dou indulged his brutality, while Yunqi often refused to go along.

sentences.zh: 雲起又營私產，交通生獠，以規其利，軌亦對眾言之，由是構隙，情相猜貳。

translations.literal: Yunqi also managed private property and trafficked with raw Liao to seek profit; Gui also spoke of this before the assembly, and thereby they built a rift, their feelings mutually doubting.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi also pursued private profit by trading with the Liao. Dou denounced this publicly, and from that their mutual suspicion grew into open enmity.

sentences.zh: 隱太子之死也，敕遣軌息馳驛詣益州報軌，軌乃疑雲起弟慶儉、堂弟慶嗣及親族並事東宮，慮其聞狀或將為變，先設備而後告之。

translations.literal: At the Hidden Crown Prince's death, an edict sent Gui's son by urgent relay to Yizhou to report to Gui; Gui then suspected Yunqi's younger brother Qingjian, his cousin Qingsi, and kinsmen who had all served the Eastern Palace, fearing that on hearing the news they might make trouble, and made preparations first before informing them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince died, an urgent dispatch was sent to Dou Gui in Yizhou. Dou suspected Yunqi's brother Qingjian, his cousin Qingsi, and other kinsmen who had served the Eastern Palace, fearing they might rise on hearing the news. He made preparations first, then announced it.

sentences.zh: 雲起果不信，問曰：「詔書何在？」

translations.literal: Yunqi indeed did not believe and asked, "Where is the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi refused to believe him and asked, "Where is the edict?

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「公，建成黨也，今不奉詔，同反明矣。」

translations.literal: Gui said, "Sir, you are a partisan of Jiancheng; now you do not obey the edict—rebellion together is obvious."
translations.idiomatic: Dou said, "You are a partisan of Jiancheng. Your refusal to obey the edict proves you mean to rebel."

sentences.zh: 遂執殺之。

translations.literal: He then seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yunqi seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 初，雲起年少時，師事太學博士王頗，頗每與之言及時事，甚嘉嘆之，乃謂之曰：「韋生識悟如是，必能自取富貴；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yunqi was young, he studied under the Imperial University Erudite Wang Po; Po often spoke with him of current affairs and greatly admired and sighed over him, saying to him, "Student Wei, with insight and understanding such as this, will surely obtain wealth and honor for himself;
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yunqi studied under Imperial University Erudite Wang Po, who often discussed current affairs with him and admired him greatly. Wang told him, "With understanding such as yours, Wei, you will surely win wealth and rank for yourself;

sentences.zh: 然剛腸嫉惡，終當以此害身。」

translations.literal: yet with a rigid belly that hates evil, in the end he will harm his person thereby."
translations.idiomatic: but your rigid hatred of evil will in the end destroy you.

sentences.zh: 竟如頗言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as Po had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved Wang Po right.

sentences.zh: 子師實，垂拱初，官至華州刺史、太子少詹事，封扶陽郡公。

translations.literal: His son Shishi, at the beginning of Chuigong, reached the posts of Governor of Huazhou and Junior Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Fuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi, early in the Chuigong reign, rose to Governor of Huazhou and Junior Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent and was enfeoffed as Duke of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 師實子方質，則天初鸞台侍郎、地官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Shishi's son Fangzhi, at the beginning of Zetian's reign, was Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace, Minister of the Earth Office, and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace with the rank of Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi's son Fangzhi, early in Empress Wu's reign, served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace, Minister of the Earth Office, and Grand Counselor of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 時改修《垂拱格式》，方質多所損益，甚為時人所稱。

translations.literal: At that time the Chuigong Statutes and Formats were being revised; Fangzhi made many additions and deletions and was greatly praised by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chuigong Statutes and Formats were revised, Fangzhi made many improvements and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 俄而武承嗣、三思當朝用事，諸宰相咸傾附之。

translations.literal: Before long Wu Chengsi and Sansi held power in court, and all the chief counselors leaned and attached themselves to them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi dominated the court, and the chief counselors all courted them.

sentences.zh: 方質疾假，承嗣等詣宅問疾，方質據床不為之禮。

translations.literal: Fangzhi was on sick leave; Chengsi and the others came to his residence to inquire after his illness, and Fangzhi sat on his bed and did not perform ceremony for them.
translations.idiomatic: While Fangzhi was on sick leave, Chengsi and the others called at his home. Fangzhi remained seated on his bed and offered them no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 左右云：「踞見權貴，恐招危禍。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said, "Sitting sprawled before the powerful and noble—fear you will invite deadly calamity."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants warned, "To sit informally before such powerful men may bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 方質曰：「吉凶命也。

translations.literal: Fangzhi said, "Fortune and misfortune are fate.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzhi said, "Fortune and misfortune are a matter of fate.

sentences.zh: 大丈夫豈能折節曲事近戚，以求苟免也。」

translations.literal: How could a great man bend his joints and crook himself to serve imperial kin, seeking to escape by compromise?"
translations.idiomatic: A true man does not bend his back to court imperial relatives merely to save his skin."

sentences.zh: 尋為酷吏周興、來子珣所構，配流儋州，仍籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was framed by the cruel officials Zhou Xing and Lai Zixun, sentenced to exile in Danzhou, and his household property was still confiscated and registered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was framed by the cruel officials Zhou Xing and Lai Zixun, exiled to Danzhou, and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 神龍初雪免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong his name was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong reign his name was cleared.

sentences.zh: 孫伏伽孫伏伽，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Sun Fuyi. Sun Fuyi was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fuyi. Sun Fuyi was from Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業末，自大理寺史累補萬年縣法曹。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, from Clerk of the Court of Review he was promoted in succession to Legal Officer of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye reign he rose from clerk of the Court of Review to Legal Officer of Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，初以三事上諫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he first remonstrated on three matters.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 1 he submitted his first remonstrance on three matters.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：

translations.literal: The first states:
translations.idiomatic: The first states:

sentences.zh: 其二曰：

translations.literal: The second states:
translations.idiomatic: The second states:

sentences.zh: 其三曰：

translations.literal: The third states:
translations.idiomatic: The third states:

sentences.zh: 高祖覽之大悅，下詔曰「秦以不聞其過而亡，典籍豈無先誡？

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor read it and was greatly pleased, issuing an edict saying, "Qin perished because it did not hear its faults—do the classics not contain prior warnings?
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor read it with great pleasure and issued an edict: "Qin perished because it would not hear its faults—is there no warning in the classics?

sentences.zh: 臣僕諂諛，故弗之覺也。

translations.literal: Ministers and servants flattered and fawned, so it did not perceive them.
translations.idiomatic: Its ministers flattered and fawned, so the ruler never perceived his errors.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖反正，從諫如流。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han restored the proper order and followed remonstrance as flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han restored order and followed remonstrance as freely as flowing water.

sentences.zh: 洎乎文、景繼業，宣、元承緒，不由斯道，孰隆景祚？

translations.literal: Down to Wen and Jing continuing the enterprise, Xuan and Yuan inheriting the thread—without this Way, who could exalt the glorious fortune?
translations.idiomatic: From Wen and Jing through Xuan and Yuan—without this Way, who could have exalted the Han fortune?

sentences.zh: 周、隋之季，忠臣結舌，一言喪邦，諒足深誡。

translations.literal: At the ends of Zhou and Sui, loyal ministers bit their tongues; one word lost the state—surely a lesson deep enough for warning.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Zhou and Sui, loyal ministers fell silent, and a single unheeded word lost the realm—a warning deep enough for any age.

sentences.zh: 永言於此，常深嘆息。

translations.literal: Speaking forever of this, I often sigh deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on this, I sigh deeply.

sentences.zh: 朕每惟寡薄，恭膺寶命，雖不能性與天道，庶思勉力，常冀弼諧，以匡不逮。

translations.literal: I constantly consider my meager thinness, reverently receiving the precious Mandate; though I cannot make my nature one with Heaven's Way, I hope to think of striving with effort, always looking for assisting harmony to correct my shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: I know how meager my talents are, yet I have reverently received the Mandate. Though I cannot align my nature with Heaven's Way, I strive with all my strength and constantly seek loyal counsel to correct my failings.

sentences.zh: 而群公卿士，罕進直言，將申虛受之懷，物所未諭。

translations.literal: Yet the host of dukes, ministers, and scholars rarely advance blunt speech; I wish to express a mind of empty receptivity, but things are not as I would explain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my ministers rarely speak blunt truth, though I wish to show an open and receptive heart—a wish the world has not understood.

sentences.zh: 萬年縣法曹孫伏伽，至誠慷慨，詞義懇切，指陳得失，無所迴避。

translations.literal: Sun Fuyi, Legal Officer of Wannian County, is utterly sincere and generous, his words and meaning earnest, pointing out gains and losses without any evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fuyi, Legal Officer of Wannian County, has spoken with utter sincerity and earnestness, setting forth right and wrong without evasion.

sentences.zh: 非有不次之舉，曷貽利行之益！

translations.literal: Unless there is an extraordinary promotion, how can the benefit of profitable conduct be bestowed!
translations.idiomatic: Without an extraordinary reward, how can the benefit of loyal conduct be shown to the realm!

sentences.zh: 伏伽既懷諒直，宜處憲司，可治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Fuyi, holding honest bluntness, should be placed in the censorate—he may serve as Attending Imperial Censor for Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyi, being honest and blunt, belongs in the censorate; appoint him Attending Imperial Censor for Documents.

sentences.zh: 仍頒示遠近，知朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Let it still be promulgated far and near, so all may know Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Let this edict be promulgated far and wide, so all may know my intent.

sentences.zh: 兼賜帛三百匹。

translations.literal: He was also granted three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，賦斂繁重，伏伽屢奏請改革，高祖並納焉。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many and levies heavy; Fuyi repeatedly memorialized requesting reforms, and the Founding Emperor accepted them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military affairs were pressing and levies heavy. Fuyi repeatedly memorialized for reform, and the Founding Emperor accepted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 二年，高祖謂裴寂曰：「隋末無道，上下相蒙，主則驕矜，臣惟諂佞。

translations.literal: In the second year the Founding Emperor said to Pei Ji, "At the end of Sui there was no Way; above and below deceived one another—the ruler was arrogant and proud, the ministers only fawning and sycophantic.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 the Founding Emperor told Pei Ji, "At the end of Sui there was no moral governance. Court and emperor deceived one another—the ruler grew arrogant, and his ministers offered only flattery.

sentences.zh: 上不聞過，下不盡忠，至使社稷傾危，身死匹夫之手。

translations.literal: Above, faults were not heard; below, loyalty was not fully given—until the altars of soil and grain toppled into danger and the body died at the hands of common men.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler would not hear his faults, and his ministers would not speak loyal truth, until the realm collapsed and the emperor died at the hands of commoners.

sentences.zh: 朕撥亂反正，志在安人，平亂任武臣，守成委文吏，庶得各展器能，以匡不逮。

translations.literal: I have swept away disorder and restored the proper, my aim to settle the people; in pacifying disorder I entrust military ministers, in guarding the accomplishment I delegate civil officials, hoping each may display his capacity to correct my shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: I have swept away disorder and restored order, aiming to settle the people. I entrust pacification to military men and governance to civil officials, so each may use his talents to correct my failings.

sentences.zh: 比每虛心接待，冀聞讜言。

translations.literal: Lately I have each time received them with an empty mind, hoping to hear blunt loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: I have received them with an open heart, hoping to hear blunt loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 然惟李綱善盡忠款，孫伏伽可謂誠直，餘人猶踵弊風，俯首而已，豈朕所望哉！」

translations.literal: Yet only Li Gang is good at fulfilling loyal sincerity; Sun Fuyi may be called sincere and upright—the rest still follow the old corrupt wind, bowing their heads and nothing more. Is this what I hoped for!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet only Li Gang has shown full loyal sincerity, and Sun Fuyi may be called honest and upright. The rest still follow the old corrupt ways, bowing their heads and nothing more—is this what I hoped for?

sentences.zh: 及平王世充、竇建德，大赦天下，既而責其黨與，並令配遷。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande were pacified, a great amnesty was proclaimed for the realm; afterward their partisans were blamed and all ordered to exile and relocation.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande were defeated, a general amnesty was proclaimed; afterward their partisans were punished and ordered into exile.

sentences.zh: 伏伽上表諫曰：

translations.literal: Fuyi submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fuyi submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 又上表請置諫官，高祖皆納焉。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of remonstrating officials; the Founding Emperor accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized for the establishment of remonstrating officials, and the Founding Emperor accepted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，賜爵樂安縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he was granted the title Baron of Le'an County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Fuyi was granted the title Baron of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，轉大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 1 he was made Vice Minister of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗馬射，伏伽上書諫曰：「臣聞千金之子，坐不垂堂；

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once shot from horseback; Fuyi submitted a written remonstrance, saying, "Your subject has heard that the son of a thousand gold pieces does not sit with his feet hanging over the hall;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong once shot from horseback, Fuyi remonstrated in writing: "I have heard that the son of a man worth a thousand gold pieces does not sit with his feet over the edge of the hall;

sentences.zh: 百金之子，立不倚衡。

translations.literal: the son of a hundred gold pieces does not stand leaning on a railing.
translations.idiomatic: and the son of a man worth a hundred gold pieces does not stand leaning on a gate bar.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，天下之主，不可履險乘危明矣。

translations.literal: By this it is said, the lord of all under Heaven must not tread danger and ride peril—it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that the ruler of all under Heaven must not court danger.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞天子之居也，則禁衛九重；

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that where the Son of Heaven dwells, there are ninefold barred guards;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that where the Son of Heaven dwells, guards stand ninefold deep;

sentences.zh: 其動也，則出警入蹕。

translations.literal: when he moves, then out go the guards and in come the road-clearers.
translations.idiomatic: and when he moves, guards go before and road-clearers follow after.

sentences.zh: 此非極尊其居處，乃為社稷生靈之大計耳。

translations.literal: this is not to the utmost honor his dwelling, but is the great plan for the altars of state and the living masses.
translations.idiomatic: This is not merely to exalt his dwelling, but the great plan for the realm and its people.

sentences.zh: 故古人云：『一人有慶，兆人賴之。』

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients said, 'When one man has blessing, the myriad people rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said, 'When one man prospers, the myriad people benefit.

sentences.zh: 臣竊聞陛下猶自走馬射帖，娛悅近臣，此乃無禁乘危，竊為陛下有所不取也。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately heard that Your Majesty still personally gallops horses shooting at targets, amusing favored close ministers—this is riding peril without restraint; your subject privately holds that Your Majesty should not take this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear that Your Majesty still gallops and shoots at targets to amuse favored courtiers. This is to ride peril without restraint, and I beg Your Majesty not to do it.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 一則非光史冊，二則未足顯揚，又非所以導養聖躬，亦不可以垂範後代。

translations.literal: First, it does not glorify the historical records; second, it is insufficient to display and exalt; moreover it is not the means to guide and nurture the sacred person, nor can it be handed down as a model to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: First, it brings no glory to the historical record; second, it displays no true excellence; third, it does not nurture Your Majesty's sacred person; and fourth, it cannot serve as a model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 此只是少年諸王之所務，豈得既為天子，今日猶行之乎？

translations.literal: This is only what young princes of the blood pursue—how can one who is already Son of Heaven still practice it today?
translations.idiomatic: This is the pastime of young princes—how can the Son of Heaven still practice it today?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲自輕，其奈社稷天下何！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty may wish to make light of yourself, what of the altars of state and all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty may wish to take risks upon himself, what of the realm and the altars of state!

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，竊謂不可。」

translations.literal: In your subject's foolish view, I privately hold it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, it simply cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 太宗覽之大悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong read it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong read it with great pleasure.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐奏囚誤失免官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because of an error in reporting on prisoners in a memorial, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was dismissed for an error in a memorial on prisoners.

sentences.zh: 尋起為刑部郎中，累遷大理少卿，轉民部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was reappointed Director of the Bureau of Punishments, was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Court of Review, and transferred to Vice Minister of the People Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Director of the Bureau of Punishments, then promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Review and Vice Minister of the People Department.

sentences.zh: 十四年，拜大理卿，後出為陝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Review, and later went out as Governor of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Review, and later served as Governor of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he retired because of old age.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui year 5 he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianqing year 3.

sentences.zh: 張玄素張玄素，蒲州虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuansu. Zhang Xuansu was a native of Yuxiang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuansu. Zhang Xuansu was from Yuxiang in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋末，為景城縣戶曹。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he was Revenue Clerk of Jingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui he served as Revenue Clerk of Jingcheng County.

sentences.zh: 竇建德攻陷景城，玄素被執，將就戮，縣民千餘人號泣請代其命，曰：「此人清慎若是，今倘殺之，乃無天也。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande captured Jingcheng; Xuansu was seized and about to be executed; more than a thousand county people wept and begged to die in his place, saying, "This man's purity and caution are such—if he is killed now, there is no Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande captured Jingcheng, Xuansu was seized for execution. More than a thousand townspeople wept and begged to die in his place, saying, "This man is so upright and careful that to kill him would be to deny Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 大王將定天下，當深加禮接，以招四方，如何殺之，使善人解體？」

translations.literal: Great King, you are about to settle all under Heaven—you should deeply honor and receive him to summon the four quarters; how can you kill him and make good men lose heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Great King, you are about to settle the realm and should honor such men to win the four quarters. How can you kill him and make the good lose heart?

sentences.zh: 建德遽命釋之，署為治書侍御史，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Jiande immediately ordered him released and appointed him Attending Imperial Censor for Documents, but he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande at once ordered him released and offered him the post of Attending Imperial Censor for Documents, but Xuansu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 及江都不守，又召拜黃門侍郎，始應命。

translations.literal: When Jiangdu fell, he was again summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate; only then did he accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangdu fell, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 建德平，授景城都督府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Jiande was pacified, he was appointed Recording Advisor of the Jingcheng Area Command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande was defeated, he was appointed Recording Advisor at the Jingcheng Area Command.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，及即位，召見，訪以政道。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong heard his name, and when he took the throne summoned him for an audience and inquired of him concerning the Way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had heard of him, and on taking the throne summoned him and asked his views on governance.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣觀自古以來，未有如隋室喪亂之甚，豈非其君自專，其法日亂。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject observes that from antiquity until now there has been nothing like the extremity of Sui's mourning and disorder—is it not because its ruler monopolized power and its laws daily fell into chaos?
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In all history I have seen nothing like the ruin of the Sui. Was it not because its ruler monopolized power while its laws fell daily into chaos?

sentences.zh: 向使君虛受於上，臣弼違於下，豈至於此？

translations.literal: Had the ruler emptily received above and ministers assisted and remonstrated below, how could it have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Had the ruler been receptive above and his ministers loyal and remonstrant below, how could it have come to this?

sentences.zh: 且萬乘之重，又欲自專庶務，日斷十事而五條不中，中者信善，其如不中者何？

translations.literal: Moreover, with the weight of ten thousand chariots, yet wishing to monopolize all common affairs, deciding ten matters a day while five miss the mark—the hits are truly good, but what of the misses?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, bearing the weight of empire, he still wished to decide every affair himself. If he judged ten matters a day and five were wrong, the five right ones might be good—but what of the five wrong ones?

sentences.zh: 況一日萬機，己多虧失，以日繼月，乃至累年，乖謬既多，不亡何待！

translations.literal: How much more when in one day ten thousand affairs—how many losses already! Day following month, even to accumulated years—with so many errors, what wait for not perishing!
translations.idiomatic: And when ten thousand affairs press upon a single day, how many more errors accumulate! Day after day, month after month, year after year—with so many mistakes, how could the dynasty not perish?

sentences.zh: 如其廣任賢良，高居深視，百司奉職，誰敢犯之？

translations.literal: If he broadly entrusted the worthy and good, dwelt high and looked deep, and the hundred offices fulfilled their duties—who would dare offend?
translations.idiomatic: Had he broadly entrusted the worthy, dwelt aloft and looked deep, and let the hundred offices fulfill their duties—who would have dared offend?

sentences.zh: 臣又觀隋末沸騰，被於宇縣，所爭天下者不過十數人，余皆保邑全身，思歸有道。

translations.literal: Your subject further observes that at the end of Sui turmoil boiled, spreading through the realm; those contending for the realm were no more than a dozen men—the rest all guarded their towns and preserved their persons, thinking to return to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I further observe that at the end of Sui turmoil spread through the realm, yet those contending for empire were no more than a dozen men. The rest guarded their towns and longed to return to righteous rule.

sentences.zh: 是知人欲背主為亂者鮮矣，但人君不能安之，遂致於亂。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that people wishing to turn their backs on their lord and make disorder are few; only the ruler could not settle them, and so disorder was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Thus few people truly wished to rebel; it was only that their rulers could not settle them, and so disorder followed.

sentences.zh: 陛下若近覽危亡，日慎一日，堯、舜之道，何以能加！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty closely surveys peril and extinction, daily more cautious by a day—how could the Way of Yao and Shun be added to!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty keeps recent ruin in view and grows daily more cautious, what could surpass the way of Yao and Shun!

sentences.zh: 太宗善其對，擢拜侍御史，尋遷給事中。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong approved his answer and promoted him to Attending Censor, then shortly transferred him to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his answer, promoted him to Attending Censor, and soon made him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，詔發卒修洛陽宮乾陽殿，以備巡幸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan an edict mobilized laborers to repair the Qianyang Hall of the Luoyang Palace in preparation for imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 4 an edict mobilized laborers to repair the Qianyang Hall of the Luoyang Palace for imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 玄素上書諫曰：

translations.literal: Xuansu submitted a written remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu remonstrated in writing:

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「卿謂我不如煬帝，何如桀、紂？」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said, "You hold that I am not equal to Emperor Yang—how do I compare with Jie and Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "You think me no better than Emperor Yang—how then do I compare with Jie and Zhou of old?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若此殿卒興，所謂同歸於亂。

translations.literal: He replied, "If this hall is suddenly raised, it is what is called returning together to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If this hall is suddenly built, we shall share the same end in disorder.

sentences.zh: 且陛下初平東都，太上皇敕大殿高門並宜焚燬，陛下以瓦木可用，不宜焚灼，請賜與貧人。
