translations.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty first pacified the Eastern Capital, the Retired Emperor ordered that the great halls and high gates should all be burned; Your Majesty held that tiles and timber could be used and should not be burned, and requested they be given to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first pacified the Eastern Capital, the Retired Emperor ordered the great halls and high gates burned. Your Majesty said the tiles and timber could still be used and should be given to the poor instead.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，然天下翕然謳歌至德。

translations.literal: Though the matter did not go through, yet all under Heaven harmoniously sang hymns to supreme virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Though the order was not carried out, all under Heaven sang of your supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 今若遵舊制，即是隋役復興。

translations.literal: Now if the old system is followed, this is the corvée labor of Sui reviving.
translations.idiomatic: To follow the old ways now would be to revive the forced labor of Sui.

sentences.zh: 五六年間，趨舍頓異，何以昭示子孫，光敷四海？」

translations.literal: Within five or six years, turning and lodging suddenly differ—how can this be shown to descendants and spread its light through the four seas?"
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years your course has changed so sharply—how can this be shown to posterity or spread your light to the four seas?"

sentences.zh: 太宗嘆曰：「我不思量，遂至於此。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong sighed and said, "I did not think it through, and so came to this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sighed. "I did not think it through, and came to this."

sentences.zh: 顧謂房玄齡曰：「洛陽土中，朝貢道均，朕故修營，意在便於百姓。

translations.literal: Turning to Fang Xuanling he said, "Luoyang is central in the soil; the tribute routes are even—I therefore repair and build, my intent to benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Fang Xuanling and said, "Luoyang lies at the center of the realm and the tribute routes are even. I meant this repair to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 今玄素上表，實亦可依，後必事理須行，露坐亦復何苦，所有作役，宜即停之。

translations.literal: Now Xuansu's memorial can truly be followed; later when affairs require it, it must be done—even sitting in the open air, what hardship is there? All corvée labor should immediately be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu's memorial can be followed. When the time comes we may build again—even an open-air seat would suffice. Stop all the labor at once.

sentences.zh: 然以卑干尊，古來不易，非其忠直，安能若此？

translations.literal: Yet for the lowly to interfere with the exalted has from antiquity not been easy—were it not for his loyalty and bluntness, how could he be like this?
translations.idiomatic: For the lowly to remonstrate with the exalted has never been easy. Without such loyalty and bluntness, who could do as he has done?

sentences.zh: 可賜彩二百匹。」

translations.literal: He may be granted two hundred bolts of colored silk."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him two hundred bolts of colored silk."

sentences.zh: 侍中魏徵嘆曰：「張公論事，遂有回天之力，可謂仁人之言，其利博哉！」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Chief Wei Zheng sighed and said, "Master Zhang's discussion of affairs has the power to turn back Heaven—it may be called the words of a benevolent man, whose benefit is vast!"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Chief Wei Zheng sighed and said, "Master Zhang's words have the power to turn Heaven itself around. These are the words of a benevolent man, and their benefit is vast!"

sentences.zh: 累遷太子少詹事，轉右庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Junior Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Right Vice President of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent, then to Right Vice President of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 時承乾居春宮，頗以游畋廢學，玄素上書諫曰：「臣聞皇天無親，惟德是輔，苟違天道，人神同棄。

translations.literal: At that time Chenghan dwelt in the Eastern Palace and largely abandoned study for excursion and hunting; Xuansu submitted a written remonstrance, saying, "Your subject has heard that High Heaven has no favorites—only virtue is assisted; if one violates Heaven's Way, men and spirits alike abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: While Chenghan dwelt in the Eastern Palace he largely abandoned study for hunting and pleasure. Xuansu remonstrated in writing: "I have heard that High Heaven has no favorites and assists only virtue. Whoever violates Heaven's Way is abandoned by men and spirits alike.

sentences.zh: 然古三驅之禮，非欲教殺，將為百姓除害，故湯羅一面，天下歸仁。

translations.literal: Yet the ancient rite of three drives was not meant to teach killing, but to remove harm for the common people; therefore when Tang netted on three sides, all under Heaven returned to humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient rite of three drives was not meant to teach killing but to remove harm from the people. When Tang left one side of the net open, the realm turned to humaneness.

sentences.zh: 今苑中娛獵，雖名異游畋，若行之無常，終虧雅度。

translations.literal: Now hunting for pleasure in the park, though called a different sort of excursion and hunt, if practiced without constancy will in the end injure elegant measure.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting for pleasure in the park, though called a refined sport, practiced without restraint will in the end diminish your dignity.

sentences.zh: 且傅說曰：『學不師古，匪說攸聞。』

translations.literal: Moreover Fu Yue said, 'In study, not taking antiquity as teacher—this is not what Fu Yue has heard.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yue said, 'Learning without taking antiquity as teacher is something I have never heard of.

sentences.zh: 然則弘道在於學古，學古必資師訓。

translations.literal: Thus to expand the Way lies in studying antiquity, and studying antiquity must rely on teachers' instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Thus to enlarge the Way one must study antiquity, and to study antiquity one must rely on teachers.

sentences.zh: 既奉恩詔，令孔穎達侍講，望數存問，以補萬一。

translations.literal: Having received the gracious edict appointing Kong Yingda to attend and lecture, I hope you will frequently inquire after him, to supplement the one in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: You have already been graced with Kong Yingda as lecturer. I beg you to inquire after him frequently, that he may supply what is lacking.

sentences.zh: 仍博遣有名行學士，兼朝夕侍奉。

translations.literal: Still broadly send famous scholars of conduct and learning, also attending morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Send also other scholars of renown and integrity to attend you morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 覽聖人之遺教，察既行之往事，日知其所不足，月無忘其所能。

translations.literal: Peruse the sages' handed-down teachings, examine deeds already done in the past, daily know what is insufficient, monthly forget not what one is able.
translations.idiomatic: Read the teachings of the sages, examine deeds of the past, daily learn what you lack, and monthly forget not what you have mastered.

sentences.zh: 此則盡善盡美，夏啟、周誦，焉足言哉！

translations.literal: This then is utmost good and utmost beauty—how are Xia Qi and Zhou Song worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: This is true perfection—what are Xia Qi and Zhou Song beside it!

sentences.zh: 夫為人上者，未有不求其善，但以性不勝情，耽惑成亂。

translations.literal: For one who is above others, there is none who does not seek his good—but when nature cannot overcome emotion, indulgence and delusion become disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stand above others always wish to do right, but when feeling overcomes nature, indulgence becomes disorder.

sentences.zh: 耽惑既甚，忠言遂塞，所以臣下苟順，君道漸虧。

translations.literal: When indulgence and delusion are extreme, loyal words are blocked; therefore subordinates comply in perfunctory fashion and the ruler's Way daily declines.
translations.idiomatic: When indulgence grows extreme, loyal words are shut out, subordinates merely comply, and the ruler's Way daily declines.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『勿以小惡而不去，小善而不為。』

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: 'Do not leave a small evil because it is small, nor fail to do a small good because it is small.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'Do not leave a small evil undone because it is small, nor neglect a small good because it is small.

sentences.zh: 故知禍福之來，皆起於漸。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the coming of fortune and calamity all arise from gradualness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus fortune and calamity alike arise from gradual change.

sentences.zh: 殿下地居儲兩，當須廣樹嘉猷。

translations.literal: Your Highness occupies the position of stored succession—you should broadly plant fine plans.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness stands in the position of heir—you must broadly plant fine counsel.

sentences.zh: 既有好畋之淫，何以主斯匕鬯？

translations.literal: Having already the excess of loving the hunt, how can you preside over these sacrificial ladles and spirits?
translations.idiomatic: If you indulge in hunting, how can you preside over the ancestral sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 慎終如始，猶懼漸衰，始尚不慎，終將安保！」

translations.literal: To be careful at the end as at the beginning—one still fears gradual decline; if at the start one is not yet careful, in the end how will it be secured!
translations.idiomatic: To be careful at the end as at the beginning still leaves fear of gradual decline. If you are careless at the start, how can the end be secure!

sentences.zh: 尋又兼太子少詹事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he also concurrently served as Junior Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also served concurrently as Junior Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又上書諫曰：「臣聞周公以大聖之材，猶握髮吐飧，引納白屋，而況後之聖賢，敢輕斯道？

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he again submitted a written remonstrance, saying, "Your subject has heard that the Duke of Zhou, with the talent of a great sage, still grasped his hair and spat out his meal, drawing in men from humble thatched roofs—how much more later sages and worthies—who would dare make light of this Way?
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he remonstrated again in writing: "I have heard that the Duke of Zhou, though a great sage, still grasped his disheveled hair and spat out his food to receive men from humble roofs. How much more must later sages honor this Way!

sentences.zh: 是以禮制皇太子入學而行齒胄，欲使太子知君臣、父子、長幼之道。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual regulated that the Imperial Heir Apparent enter school and perform the cap-and-teeth ceremony, wishing to make the heir know the Way of ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ritual required the heir apparent to enter school and perform the cap ceremony, that he might learn the Way of ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger.

sentences.zh: 然君臣之義、父子之親、尊卑之序、長幼之節，用之方寸之內，弘之四海之外，皆因行以遠聞，假言以光被。

translations.literal: Yet the righteousness of ruler and minister, the intimacy of father and son, the order of honor and lowliness, the propriety of elder and younger—applied within a square inch, extended beyond the four seas—all rely on conduct to be heard afar and borrow words to spread their radiance.
translations.idiomatic: The duties of ruler and minister, the bonds of father and son, the order of rank, the propriety of age—applied within the heart and extended to the four seas—are heard afar through conduct and spread through words.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下睿質已隆，尚須學文以飾其表。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Highness's keen substance is already lofty, yet still needs to study literature to adorn its outward show.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's native brilliance is already lofty, yet you still need literary study to adorn it outwardly.

sentences.zh: 至如孔穎達、趙弘智等，非惟宿德鴻儒，亦兼達政要，望令數得侍講，開釋物理，覽古諭今，增暉睿德。

translations.literal: As for Kong Yingda, Zhao Hongzhi, and the like—they are not only elders of virtue and great ru scholars, but also understand the essentials of governance; I hope you will order them frequently to attend and lecture, opening and explaining principle and things, surveying antiquity to instruct the present, adding radiance to keen virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Kong Yingda and Zhao Hongzhi are not only eminent scholars but understand the essentials of governance. I beg that they lecture you frequently, expounding principle, surveying antiquity to instruct the present, and adding luster to your brilliance.

sentences.zh: 而彫蟲小伎之流，只可時命追隨，以代博弈耳。

translations.literal: As for the stream of decorative insect trifles and petty skills, they may only be summoned from time to time to follow along, to replace board games—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Men skilled only in decorative trifles may be summoned occasionally to replace games at chess—that is all.

sentences.zh: 若其騎射畋游，酣歌戲玩，以悅耳目，終穢心神，漸染既久，必移情性。

translations.literal: If one rides, shoots, hunts, and roams, sings drunkenly and plays with toys to please the eyes and ears—in the end the spirit is defiled; gradual dyeing over long time will surely shift disposition and nature.
translations.idiomatic: But riding, shooting, hunting, drunken song, and idle play please only the senses and in the end defile the spirit. Long indulgence will surely alter your nature.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『心為萬事主，動而無節即亂。』

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: 'The heart is master of the ten thousand affairs; movement without measure is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'The heart is master of all affairs; movement without restraint is disorder.

sentences.zh: 臣恐殿下敗德之源，在於此矣。」

translations.literal: Your subject fears that the source of Your Highness's failing virtue lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the source of Your Highness's moral failure lies here.

sentences.zh: 承乾並不能納。

translations.literal: Chenghan could not accept any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghan would accept none of it.

sentences.zh: 太宗知玄素在東宮頻有進諫，十四年，擢授銀青光祿大夫，行太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong knew that Xuansu in the Eastern Palace frequently advanced remonstrances; in the fourteenth year he was promoted and granted Silver Blue-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting as Left Vice President of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how often Xuansu had remonstrated in the Eastern Palace, Emperor Taizong in year 14 promoted him to Silver Blue-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Left Vice President of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 時承乾久不坐朝，玄素諫曰：「宮內止有婦人耳，不知如樊姬之徒，可與弘益聖德者有幾？

translations.literal: At that time Chenghan had long not presided at court; Xuansu remonstrated, saying, "Within the palace there are only women—I do not know how many like Lady Fan Ji there are who can expand and benefit sacred virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghan had long ceased to attend court. Xuansu remonstrated: "Within the palace there are only women. How many among them are like Lady Fan Ji, who could enlarge your virtue?

sentences.zh: 若遂無賢哲，便是親嬖倖，遠忠良。

translations.literal: If in the end there are no worthy and wise, this is to be intimate with favorites and keep the loyal and good at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: If there are no wise women, you draw close to favorites and keep the loyal at a distance.

sentences.zh: 人不見德，何以光敷三善？

translations.literal: If others do not see your virtue, how can you spread radiance on the three excellences?
translations.idiomatic: If others do not see your virtue, how can you spread the three excellences of the heir apparent?

sentences.zh: 且宮儲之寄，於國為重，所以廣置群僚，以輔睿德。

translations.literal: Moreover, the charge of the palace succession is weighty for the state; therefore many officials are broadly appointed to assist keen virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the heir apparent's charge is weighty for the state. That is why many officials are appointed to assist your brilliance.

sentences.zh: 今乃動經時月，不見宮臣，納誨既疏，將何補闕？」

translations.literal: Now for months on end the palace officials are not seen; receiving admonition is already sparse—how will deficiencies be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for months on end you do not see your palace officials. Admonition grows sparse—how will your failings be corrected?

sentences.zh: 承乾嫉其數諫，遣戶奴夜以馬撾擊之，殆至於死。

translations.literal: Chenghan resented his repeated remonstrances and sent a household slave by night to strike him with a horse whip, nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghan resented his repeated remonstrances and sent a household slave to beat him at night with a horse whip, nearly killing him.

sentences.zh: 承乾又嘗於宮中擊鼓，聲聞於外，玄素叩閣請見，極言切諫，承乾乃出宮內鼓，對玄素毀之。

translations.literal: Chenghan also once beat drums within the palace until the sound was heard outside; Xuansu knocked at the gate and requested an audience, speaking with extreme blunt remonstrance; Chenghan then brought out the palace drums and destroyed them before Xuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghan once beat drums in the palace until the sound carried outside. Xuansu knocked at the gate and remonstrated bluntly. Chenghan brought out the drums and smashed them before Xuansu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太宗嘗對朝問玄素歷官所由，玄素既出自刑部令史，甚以慚恥。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Taizong once faced the court and asked Xuansu the origin of his official career; Xuansu, having come from a clerk of the Ministry of Punishments, was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Taizong asked Xuansu in court about his career origins. Xuansu, who had begun as a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良上疏曰：「臣聞君子不失言於人，聖主不戲言於臣。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Grand Master Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial, saying, "Your subject has heard that the gentleman does not speak carelessly to others, and the sage ruler does not jest in speech to his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Grand Master Chu Suiliang memorialized: "I have heard that a gentleman does not speak lightly to others, and a sage ruler does not jest with his ministers.

sentences.zh: 言則史書之，禮成之，樂歌之。

translations.literal: When he speaks, the historians record it; ritual completes it; music hymns it.
translations.idiomatic: His words are recorded by historians, enshrined in ritual, and hymned in music.

sentences.zh: 居上能禮其臣，臣始能盡力以奉其上。

translations.literal: When one above can treat his ministers with ritual, ministers then can exhaust their strength to serve their superior.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler treats his ministers with respect, they can exhaust their strength in his service.

sentences.zh: 近代宋孝武輕言肆口，侮弄朝臣，攻其門戶，乃至狼狽。

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Xiaowu of Song spoke lightly and ran riot with his mouth, insulting and toying with court ministers, attacking their family lines, even to disgrace and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Emperor Xiaowu of Song spoke lightly and insulted his ministers, attacking their family lines even to disgrace.

sentences.zh: 良史書之，以為非是。

translations.literal: Good historians recorded it and held it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Good historians recorded this and judged it wrong.

sentences.zh: 陛下昨見問張玄素云：『隋任何官？』

translations.literal: Yesterday Your Majesty in audience asked Zhang Xuansu, saying, 'What office did you hold under Sui?'
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Your Majesty asked Zhang Xuansu what office he held under Sui.

sentences.zh: 奏云：『縣尉。』

translations.literal: He memorialized, 'County vice-magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'County vice-magistrate.'

sentences.zh: 又問：『未為縣尉已前？』

translations.literal: You again asked, 'Before you were county vice-magistrate?
translations.idiomatic: You asked again, 'Before that?'

sentences.zh: 奏云：『流外。』

translations.literal: He memorialized, 'Outside the regular stream.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'An irregular clerk.'

sentences.zh: 又問：『在何曹司？』

translations.literal: You again asked, 'In which bureau and office?
translations.idiomatic: You asked again which bureau he had served in.

sentences.zh: 玄素將出閣門，殆不能移步，精爽頓盡，色類死灰。

translations.literal: As Xuansu was about to leave the Gate Pavilion, he could barely move his steps; his spirit was suddenly exhausted and his complexion like dead ashes.
translations.idiomatic: As Xuansu left the Gate Pavilion he could barely walk; his spirit collapsed and his face turned ashen.

sentences.zh: 朝臣見之，多所驚怪。

translations.literal: The court ministers who saw it were mostly startled and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers who saw him were greatly astonished.

sentences.zh: 大唐創歷，任官以才；

translations.literal: Great Tang established its calendar—appointing office by talent;
translations.idiomatic: Since Great Tang established its rule, offices have been filled by talent;

sentences.zh: 卜祝庸保，量能使用。

translations.literal: diviners, prayer-officers, menials and guards—all are used according to measured capacity.
translations.idiomatic: even diviners, prayer-officers, and menials are employed according to their capacity.

sentences.zh: 陛下禮重玄素，頻年任使，擢授三品，翼贊皇儲，自不可更對群臣，窮其門戶，棄昔日之殊恩，成一朝之愧恥。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has treated Xuansu with ritual honor, repeatedly employing him over years, promoting him to the third rank, assisting the imperial heir—you naturally cannot again face the host of ministers and exhaust his family line, casting aside former special grace and making a single morning's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has honored Xuansu with repeated appointments, raised him to the third rank, and set him to assist the heir apparent. You cannot now interrogate his origins before the whole court, casting aside your former favor and turning it into a morning's humiliation.

sentences.zh: 人君之御臣下也，禮義以導之，惠澤以驅之，使其負戴玄天，罄輸臣節，猶恐德禮不加，人不自勵。

translations.literal: When the ruler guides his ministers below, he leads them with ritual and righteousness and drives them with favor and grace, making them bear the dark Heaven on their backs and pour out their full ministerial devotion—yet he still fears that if virtue and ritual are not applied, men will not spur themselves on.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler guides his ministers with ritual and righteousness and drives them with favor and grace, that they may bear Heaven on their backs and pour out loyal service—yet even then he fears that without virtue and ritual they will not strive of themselves.

sentences.zh: 若無故忽略，使其羞慚，鬱結於懷，衷心靡樂，責其伏節死義，其可得乎？」

translations.literal: If without cause he is neglected, making him ashamed, knotting grief in his breast, his loyal heart without joy—how can one demand that he hide his integrity and die for righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: If without cause you slight him to shame, knotting grief in his heart and leaving his loyal spirit joyless, how can you then demand that he die for righteousness?

sentences.zh: 書奏，太宗謂遂良曰：「朕亦悔此問，今得卿疏，深會我心。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Taizong said to Suiliang, "I too regret this questioning; now receiving your memorial, it deeply meets my heart."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Taizong told Suiliang, "I too regret this questioning. Your memorial deeply meets my heart."

sentences.zh: 承乾既敗德日增，玄素又上書諫曰：

translations.literal: As Chenghan's failing virtue daily increased, Xuansu again submitted a written remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: As Chenghan's moral failures daily increased, Xuansu remonstrated again in writing:

sentences.zh: 書入，承乾不納，乃遣刺客將加屠害。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Chenghan would not accept it and sent assassins to add slaughter and harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Chenghan refused it and sent assassins to kill him.

sentences.zh: 俄屬宮廢，玄素隨例除史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, when the palace was abolished, Xuansu was dismissed from office according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was abolished soon after, Xuansu was dismissed according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起授潮州刺史，轉鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was reappointed Governor of Chaozhou, then transferred to Governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was reappointed Governor of Chaozhou, then transferred to Governor of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: During Yonghui he retired because of old age.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，加授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longshuo he was additionally granted Silver Blue-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo year 3 he was granted Silver Blue-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Linde he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Linde year 1.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：伏伽上疏於高祖，玄素進言於太宗，從疏賤以干至尊，懷切直以明正理，可謂至難矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The historiographer says—Fuyi submitted a memorial to the Founding Emperor, Xuansu advanced words to Emperor Taizong; from humble and lowly station to approach the utmost exalted, bearing blunt sincerity to clarify correct principle—this may be called the utmost difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer comments: Sun Fuyi memorialized the Founding Emperor and Zhang Xuansu remonstrated with Emperor Taizong—from humble station to address the throne, with blunt sincerity to clarify right principle—this was the utmost difficulty.

sentences.zh: 既而並見抽獎，咸蒙顧遇。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward both were seen promoted and rewarded, all receiving favored treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both were soon promoted and richly favored.

sentences.zh: 自非下情忠到，效匪躬之節，上聽聰明，致如流之美，孰能至於此乎？

translations.literal: Unless loyalty below reached fullness, effecting the integrity of not sparing oneself, and the ruler above listened with intelligence, achieving the beauty of following like flowing water—who could arrive at this?
translations.idiomatic: Had loyalty below not been complete, had ministers not spared themselves, and had the ruler above not listened with intelligence and followed remonstrance as flowing water—who could have achieved this?

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。」

translations.literal: The Documents says, 'Wood that follows the line is made straight; a ruler who follows remonstrance is made sage.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, 'Wood follows the plumb line and becomes straight; a ruler follows remonstrance and becomes sage.'

sentences.zh: 斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: This is what was meant.

sentences.zh: 世長幼而聰悟，長能規諫；

translations.literal: Shichang was clever and perceptive in youth, and grown could remonstrate and advise;
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was clever from youth and grew adept at remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 雲起屏絕朋黨，罔避驕豪。

translations.literal: Yunqi barred and cut off cliques, never avoiding the arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi rooted out cliques and never shrank from the arrogant and powerful.

sentences.zh: 歷覽言行，咸有可觀。

translations.literal: Surveying their words and conduct throughout, all had what was worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing their words and conduct, all had merit.

sentences.zh: 而雲起吐茹無方，世長終成詭詐，其不令也宜哉！

translations.literal: Yet Yunqi's spitting and swallowing had no method, and Shichang in the end became deceitful and fraudulent—their lack of excellence is fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yunqi was inconsistent in his judgments, and Shichang ended in deceit—small wonder they did not finish well!

sentences.zh: 方諸孫、張二子，知不迨矣。

translations.literal: Compared with Sun and the two Zhangs, their wisdom does not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Sun Fuyi and the two Zhangs, they do not measure up.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：言為身文，感義忘身。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Words are the pattern of the person; moved by righteousness, one forgets the self.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Words are the ornament of the person; moved by righteousness, one forgets the self.

sentences.zh: 不有忠膽，安輕逆鱗？

translations.literal: Without loyal gall, how dare one lightly go against the inverted scales?
translations.idiomatic: Without loyal courage, who would lightly touch the dragon's scales?

sentences.zh: 蘇、韋果俊，伽、素忠純。

translations.literal: Su and Wei were truly outstanding; Jia and Su were loyal and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Wei were truly outstanding; Sun and Zhang were loyal and pure.

sentences.zh: 悟主匡失，猗歟諍臣。

translations.literal: Awakening their lords and correcting errors—ah, the remonstrating ministers!
translations.idiomatic: They awakened their lords and corrected their faults—ah, the remonstrating ministers!
